function: ISACformer (Transformer DNN) designs the predictive transmit beamformer from past estimated CSI, trading worst-case secrecy rate of users against the CRLB of UAV eavesdroppers (p. 2, 7-8).
system: Full-duplex mono-static ISAC BS with 8x8 transmit and 8x8 receive UPAs, K=2 users with 4x4 antennas, Q=2 single-antenna UAV eavesdroppers, LoS, 28 GHz, no RIS (p. 3, 11).
method: Unsupervised ISACformer: CNN modules, 8-head attention encoder, CNN-based decoder implicitly predicting CSI; loss is the Lagrangian objective over 10000 Monte Carlo runs; offline training, online testing (p. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom MATLAB simulation: LoS channels with UPA steering vectors, Swerling I echoes, Gaussian kinematic-state noise; 7000/2000/1000 train/validation/test samples; no 3GPP model or measured data (p. 3-5, 10).
test_conditions: Trained, validated, tested on separate Monte Carlo samples of one setting; sweeps over SNR, weight factor, Lagrange multiplier, numbers of Eves and Bobs; no mismatched test (p. 10-14).
baselines: Learned: CNN+LSTM [39] and LSTM+Attention [40] predictive beamformers; non-learned: naive gradient descent and random beamformer; plus an upper bound that ignores multi-user interference (p. 11).
metrics: Ergodic worst-case secrecy rate, square root of CRLB for azimuth, elevation, distance, velocity, power-constraint satisfaction, inference time (p. 11-13).
complexity: Measured runtime only: gradient descent about 14 s versus ISACformer about 0.2 s per SNR value, roughly 70 times faster; no FLOPs or parameter count (p. 11).
openness: none; simulations in MATLAB R2024a and PyTorch, no code or data link (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 3: "point target model between all links" (LoS propagation, custom steering-vector channel); p. 10: "The datasets are obtained from simulation in MATLAB R2024a." No 3GPP model, public dataset, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "size of the training, validation, and test sets are set to 7000, 2000, and 1000, respectively", so the test set is a held-out part of the same simulation. Figs. 5-10 (p. 11-14) sweep SNR, rho, mu, Q and K; no model is tested outside its training setting.
q3_support: p. 11: "Compared to other DNN methods, such as CNN+LSTM and LSTM+Attention" and "compared to the conventional method, namely Naive Gradient Descent, our method exhibits superior performance" (worst-case SR and CRLB, Fig. 5).
q4_support: p. 11: "ISACformer only needs about 0.2 seconds per SNR value during its inference process", versus about 14 seconds for the conventional method; no FLOPs or parameter count is given.
q5_support: p. 10: "The datasets are obtained from simulation in MATLAB R2024a." No link, DOI, or public dataset is given and no code release is stated.
notes: ISAC beamforming (area 5): the learned ISACformer outputs the predictive beamformer that balances worst-case secrecy rate and CRLB; the anti-eavesdropping goal belongs to the communication objective, not a separate excluded function. The upper bound is a variant of the method and is not counted as a baseline. q3 uses CNN+LSTM [39] and LSTM+Attention [40] as learned baselines and naive gradient descent as non-learned. q4 rests on a measured runtime.
